model: Bank FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity on tangible book (engine route; residual-income equivalent: GAAP earnings after regulatory capital retention, preferred stock deducted in the equity bridge, net debt zero)

equity_bridge.note: Preferred stock $1,975m at 30 Sep 2026 (Q3 2026 10-Q balance sheet), down from $2,500m after the $525m Series D redemption for cash on 15 Sep 2026; remaining dividends ~$117m/yr. Deducted at book because the flows are total net income before preferred dividends.

historical_growth.fcf_series_note: For a bank the distributable-earnings series is GAAP net income (already after share-based compensation): FY2020 1,343 (COVID CECL build); FY2021 2,625 (reserve release, PPP fees - the peak); FY2022 1,917; FY2023 967 (deposit repricing, FDIC special assessment); FY2024 -161 (Q3-Q4 2024 securities repositioning losses of ~$900m after-tax funded by the Scotiabank capital); FY2025 1,829 (SEC XBRL NetIncomeLoss). The 5-year CAGR (6.4%) runs FY2020 trough to FY2025; the 3-year (-1.6%) runs from the FY2022 NIM peak. Revenue = NII + noninterest income (GAAP): FY2020 6,715; FY2022 7,272; FY2023 6,413; FY2024 4,619 (repositioning losses inside noninterest income; underlying ~6.0bn); FY2025 7,478. Diluted EPS FY2020 1.28, FY2022 1.94, FY2025 1.52 (share count up 19% on the Scotiabank issuance).
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Base-case 10-year average revenue growth (6.0% FY27 tapering to 2.5%), anchored on FY2026-27 guidance (NII +9-11% FY26, NIM tailwinds through 2027) rather than the 0.9-2.2% historical revenue CAGRs, which span the 2022-24 rate-shock trough and the FY2024 repositioning loss. Equity CAGRs are distorted by the $2.8bn Scotiabank issuance and AOCI swings.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3-year CAGR (14.9%) diverges >30% from revenue (0.9%) and EPS (-7.8%): book value grew through the $2.8bn Scotiabank share issuance (Aug-Dec 2024, ~163m shares) and the $4.3bn AOCI recovery from Sep 2023, not through retained earnings, so equity CAGR does not describe per-share earnings power. EPS 3-year is negative because FY2022 was the NIM peak, FY2023-24 carried deposit repricing and the repositioning loss, and the share count rose 19%. Growth is taken from the guidance and the revenue path.

scenario_narratives.base: KeyCorp delivers the guided NIM recovery - an exit-2026 NIM of ~3.00% and further fixed-rate asset repricing and swap maturities through 2027 - on ~5% loan growth, with fees compounding mid-single digits on KeyBanc Capital Markets, wealth and Clearwater UK. Expenses grow ~3.5% so the GAAP efficiency ratio improves from ~61% to ~58% and then stalls, because KeyCorp has never sustained a PNC-class cost base. Provisions normalise up from 2026's release-assisted level to ~45bp mid-cycle. GAAP EPS reaches ~$2.11 in FY2027; 66-83% of earnings are distributed. The base sits below management's reaffirmed end-2027 targets (NIM 3.25%+, ROTCE 15%+ on its own definition). At a 10.5% cost of equity the franchise is worth ~1.8x AOCI-marked tangible book ($12.35) or ~1.4x ex-AOCI tangible book, modestly above the market price.
scenario_narratives.bull: The Fed holds, the curve steepens and NIM exits 2027 above 3.20%; commercial loans grow 8-10% for a second year on deposit share gains; a multi-year M&A upcycle lifts KeyBanc/Clearwater fees 10% a year and Scotiabank cross-border referrals start to show. Positive operating leverage takes efficiency to 56% by FY2030, credit stays benign, ROTCE reaches 16-17%, FY2028 EPS clears $2.45 and the buyback runs at the full $3.0bn authorisation. Management's end-2027 targets (NIM 3.25%+, ROTCE 15%+) are met or beaten, and the market's ~9.7x forward multiple re-rates toward the 11-12x regional-bank norm.
scenario_narratives.bear: The repricing tailwind is blunted: the Fed cuts fast into a slowdown so reinvestment yields fall while deposit costs stay sticky, NIM plateaus near 2.95%, capital-markets fees drop ~20%, and loan growth stops. A mid-sized credit cycle (CRE, agriculture and consumer-goods-linked commercial exposures management already flags) pushes provisions to ~85bp in FY2028. With no operating leverage the efficiency ratio stays in the low 60s, ROTCE settles at ~10-11% - barely above the cost of equity - and the buyback is halted to rebuild marked CET1, which the Q3 2026 AOCI move has already taken to an estimated ~9.0%, below the 9.5-10% target. EPS falls to ~$1.35 before recovering slowly.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A regional bank is valued on what it can distribute after funding its regulatory capital, discounted at a USD cost of equity - never on statutory operating cash flow (which is loan and deposit movement) and never with deposits or wholesale funding treated as net debt. GAAP net income is the flow; capital retention at NPAT x g/ROTE is the reinvestment; preferred stock is deducted at book so the common claim is valued; 10.5% is the house return required from a NIM-geared US super-regional. The result is the residual-income answer in FCFE form. After Q3 2026 the weighted value is a few percent above the market price: the quarter added value through the Series D redemption and a higher revenue base, while the $1.5bn AOCI hit to tangible book changes the yardstick (1.8x marked, 1.4x ex-AOCI tangible book) rather than the distributable earnings. There is no margin of safety at the 15% hurdle, and the value is sensitive to a cost of equity that the spot 10-year would put ~0.6pt higher.
key_risks_to_valuation: Net interest margin: 5bp on ~$170bn of average earning assets is ~$85m of NII (~1.1% of revenue, ~4% of NPAT); the base assumes the guided 3.00-3.05% exit NIM and further 2027 repricing gains, and the bear case removes most of it
Credit cycle: every 10bp on the provision rate over ~$110bn of loans is ~$110m pre-tax (~4% of NPAT); CRE, agriculture and consumer-goods-linked commercial books are management's own watch categories
Capital-markets fees: investment banking and debt placement (~12% of revenue) fell ~25% peak-to-trough in 2022-23; a 20% decline is ~$190m of revenue (~7% of NPAT) with little cost offset
Operating leverage: the base assumes GAAP efficiency improves from ~61% to 58%; every 1pp is ~$85m pre-tax (~3% of NPAT), and KeyCorp's history is a ratio in the low-to-mid 60s
Cost of equity: held at the 10.5% house rate while the spot 10-year Treasury (5.07%) implies ~11.1% on the same build-up; each +0.5pt is roughly -7% of value per share (see the required-return table)

Capital: marked CET1 is an estimated ~9.0% after the Q3 2026 AOCI move (-$1.5bn), below the 9.5-10% operating range, while RWA grew 5.4% in nine months and >100% of earnings were distributed; the retention paths are unchanged, so a slower buyback or higher retention in FY2027 is unmodelled downside (each 1pt of revenue retained for three years is ~$0.2/share). A Basel III endgame re-proposal could change the RWA base either way

Scotiabank's 14.9% stake: a standstill-governed strategic holder is a stabiliser today, but any change in Scotiabank's intent (sale, or a bid) would reprice the shares in either direction outside this model

FY2026 ends 31 Dec 2026; FY0 = nine months 2026 actual 5,945 (NII 3,772 + noninterest income 2,173, Q3 2026 10-Q; Q3 alone 2,044 = 1,300 + 744) + Q4 2026E ~2,130 (NII ~1,335: guidance tightened in October 2026 to taxable-equivalent NII up ~10% on 4,671 = ~5,138 TE, ~5,105 GAAP, less 3,772; fees ~795: noninterest income guided +4-5% on 2,842 = 2,956-2,984, less 2,173). Cross-check: guided taxable-equivalent revenue up ~8% on 7,513 = ~8,114 TE = ~8,080 GAAP. Prior build (2026-09-29, on H1 actuals) carried 8,000; the +75 is Q3 landing above the run-rate assumed then (2,044 against ~2,005) and the tightened guidance. Using FY2026E as FY0 keeps year 1 = FY2027.
inputs.share_count_basis: 1,055.98m common shares outstanding at 30 Oct 2026 (Q3 2026 10-Q cover) PLUS ~9.3m dilutive awards (Q3 2026 diluted weighted average 1,064.3m vs basic 1,055.0m) = ~1,065m fully diluted. Period-end count was 1,058.2m at 30 Sep 2026 (Figure 18: 14.2m repurchased in Q3 at an average $22.57, 0.3m issued). NO estimate of repurchases after the cover date is deducted: the prior build deducted an estimated ~12m of post-cover Q3 repurchases and the actual was ~8.9m, and the remaining FY2026 programme (~$253m = ~12m shares, 'on pace' for $1.3bn against $1,047m spent in nine months) is not yet cash in financing activities. Held FLAT thereafter: share-based compensation ($100m in nine months) is expensed in the flows, so charging dilution as well would double-count; the buyback is a distribution of the FCFE the model capitalises, not a separate driver. Scotiabank's holding is in the base count (Q3 repurchases included shares bought from Scotiabank). REFRESH from the FY2026 10-K cover (due February 2027).
inputs.funding_note: Net debt is held at ZERO by construction. KeyCorp is a Fed/OCC-regulated bank holding company: long-term debt $11,473m and deposits $153,814m at 30 Sep 2026 (plus $5,185m of bank notes and short-term borrowings, and a further $1.0bn senior note issued 2 Nov 2026) are operating funding whose cost is already inside net interest income; cash and due from banks is held against that funding and is not surplus. The flow capitalised is free cash flow to equity (net income less capital retained to fund risk-weighted-asset growth at the 9.5-10% marked CET1 target) at the cost of equity, so no debt is deducted and no cash is added. total_debt is recorded for audit only. Preferred stock ($1,975m after the $525m Series D redemption on 15 Sep 2026; ~$117m/yr of dividends, down from ~$143m) is a claim senior to common and is deducted at book in equity_bridge; the flows are therefore total net income (before preferred dividends), NOT net income to common, so the preferred cost is charged exactly once. The cash that redeemed Series D is replaced by wholesale funding whose cost is charged in the flows (see margin_rationale).
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2026E FCFE = GAAP net income ~2,195 (nine months 2026 actual 1,610; Q4E ~585 = (2,130 revenue - ~1,280 noninterest expense - ~100 provision) x (1 - 22%)) LESS capital retained ~985 (~6.5% RWA growth x ~$15bn of target CET1 capital, i.e. NPAT x g/ROTE; RWA rose from $145.9bn to $153.8bn in nine months on commercial loan growth guided at ~10%). The prior build carried 1,460 on an assumed 4.5% RWA growth; FY0 FCFE is a display anchor, the valuation runs from base_revenue and the driver paths, where FY2027 RWA growth is held at 5%. Cross-check on distributions: nine-month common dividends $769m + buybacks $1,047m + the $525m preferred redemption = $2.3bn against $1.6bn of net income, i.e. well over 100% distributed, funded by running unmarked CET1 down from 11.78% to 11.08%. That is not repeatable and is not capitalised here. reported_fcf = FCFE + share-based compensation so that last_fcf = reported_fcf - sbc_incl_equity_taxes - interest_income holds.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: Statutory operating cash flow (FY2025 2,208; FY2022 4,469; Q1 2026 -62) is loan/deposit/trading movement and is meaningless as free cash flow for a bank; the CSV FreeCashFlow column is NOT used. reported_fcf here is the FCFE proxy before the SBC charge.
inputs.sbc_source: Stock-based compensation expense, consolidated statement of cash flows: nine months 2026 $100m (Q3 2026 10-Q; $99m in the prior-year period) -> ~$133m FY2026E; FY2025 $132m (10-K), FY2024 $104m, FY2023 $121m (CSV StockBasedComp). ~1.6% of revenue, so the house/street band is narrow. Employee equity-compensation share repurchases (tax withholding) were $47m in nine months and are a use of cash already covered by the SBC expense, not an additional charge.
inputs.interest_income_note: Not stripped: interest income ($9.0bn gross, $4.6bn net in FY2025) IS the banking business, and no cash is added to equity value (matching-asset rule satisfied in the other direction).
inputs.buyback_note: $320m repurchased in Q3 2026 (14.2m shares at $22.57 average, including shares bought from Scotiabank); nine months 2026 $1,047m in financing activities (Q3 2026 10-Q cash flow statement), so Q1 2026 was ~$386m, not the ~$200m the prior build estimated from cover counts. Management 'remain on pace' for $1.3bn in FY2026 (~$253m left for Q4) under the $3.0bn authorisation of May 2026, of which $2,458m remained at 30 Sep 2026. FY2022-FY2024 repurchases were nil. The flat share count is a modelling convention funded by the SBC charge in the flows; buybacks are a use of the FCFE capitalised, not an extra source of value.
inputs.share_count_date: 2026-10-30 (Q3 2026 10-Q cover count, plus Q3 dilutive awards; no post-cover repurchase estimate)
inputs.book_value_anchor: Shareholders' equity $17,809m at 30 Sep 2026 (from $19,798m at 30 Jun) less intangibles $2,814m (goodwill $2,803m after Clearwater UK, other intangibles $11m) and preferred stock $1,927m (regulatory carrying value; $1,975m on the balance sheet) = tangible common equity $13,068m = $12.35/share on 1,058.2m (company-reported; $13.63 at 30 Jun, $13.77 at 31 Dec 2025). The $1,989m fall in equity in one quarter is NOT an operating loss: AOCI moved from -$2,354m to -$3,865m (-$1,511m: available-for-sale securities -$1,188m and cash-flow hedges -$324m as the 10-year Treasury rose from ~4.3% to ~5.2% over the quarter), Series D preferred was redeemed (-$525m), and buybacks plus dividends (~$580m) roughly matched net income ($579m). AOCI of -$3,865m is ~$3.63/share that accretes back as the securities and swaps run off; ex-AOCI tangible book is ~$16.0/share. In October 2026 $2.0bn of mortgage-backed securities were moved to held-to-maturity to damp further AOCI volatility. TCE ratio 6.9% (7.7% at 30 Jun); CET1 11.08% unmarked. MARKED CET1 IS NOW AN ESTIMATED ~9.0% (CET1 capital 17,037 less AFS 2,990 and pension 233 of AOCI = 13,814 on RWA 153,761), BELOW the 9.5-10% operating target the prior build measured ~9.8% against; the company does not print the marked ratio in the 10-Q, so this is the analyst's arithmetic. ROTCE Q3 2026 15.1% (company-reported, nine months 13.7%), flattered by the lower AOCI-marked denominator and a $61m provision.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity in USD, the currency of the flows, HELD at the house rate of 10.5% used for US super-regionals (HBAN 2026-09-29): a normalised risk-free rate of 4.5% + beta 1.2 x US equity risk premium 5.0%. FLAG: the spot 10-year Treasury is 5.07% at the valuation date (Yahoo ^TNX, 18 Nov 2026) and was already ~5.2% when the prior build described 4.5% as the late-September level, so that description was a normalised rate, not the spot rate. On the spot rate the same build-up gives ~11.1%. The rate is deliberately NOT moved in this update: it is a cross-ticker house input, and moving it for one bank on a quarterly refresh would break comparability with the other bank valuations; what would move it is a house decision to re-base the bank cost of equity on a 10-year that stays at or above 5%. The effect is quantified in the required-return table and sensitivity grid (roughly -7% of value per +0.5pt). Rate-level risk is otherwise charged once: higher long rates lift reinvestment yields (the NIM path) and depress AOCI and marked capital; neither side has been re-judged here. Beta 1.2 is the measured five-year range (1.1-1.3). One rate across all three scenarios; rate-path, credit-cycle and capital-markets risk is charged in the bear flows and the 20% bear weight.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases (940 branches) are immaterial relative to $19.8bn of equity; lease cost sits inside noninterest expense and therefore inside the modelled pre-tax margin. No lease line and no lease liability deduction.
inputs.nci_treatment: No material non-controlling interests. Preferred stock (Series E-H after the Series D redemption) is the only senior equity claim and is deducted at its $1,975m balance-sheet value in equity_bridge (see funding_note), so the 21.0% cash-tax-rate driver is pure income tax (nine months 2026 effective 21.2% = 434/2,043; Q3 21.5%; FY2025 20.7%). Management guides ~22% for FY2026; the 21.0% path is left unchanged against a nine-month actual of 21.2% and would move to 22% if the FY2026 full-year rate prints there.
inputs.notes: UPDATE 2026-11-19 on the Q3 2026 10-Q (balance sheet 30 Sep 2026, cover count 30 Oct 2026); prior full build 2026-09-29. Model unchanged. CHANGED: (1) price and timestamp; (2) share count 1,064m -> 1,065m (actual cover + dilutive awards, post-cover repurchase estimate dropped); (3) preferred deduction 2,500 -> 1,975 (Series D redeemed 15 Sep 2026); (4) pre-tax margin path -0.2pt in every year of every scenario for the wholesale funding that replaced the $525m of redeemed preferred (~$24m/yr pre-tax at ~4.5%, of which only ~3.5 months is inside the FY2026E base) - a mechanical consequence of (3), not a re-judgment of efficiency or credit; (5) FY0 revenue 8,000 -> 8,075 on Q3 actuals and the tightened FY2026 guidance (NII up ~10%, revenue up ~8%, average loans up ~5%, NCOs 37-39bp from 40-45bp, exit NIM ~3.00% from 3.00-3.05%); (6) FY0 display FCFE, SBC, buyback and book-value anchors. DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED, with what would move each: growth paths in all scenarios (FY2027 base 6.0% - management's medium-term targets of NIM 3.25%+ and ROTCE 15%+ as end-2027 run rates were reaffirmed with Q3 and are above the base, which reaches ~3.1% average NIM; they are targets, not guidance, and FY2027 guidance in January 2027 is what would move the path); the underlying efficiency and provision judgments (Q3 efficiency 60.9%, provision $61m = 3.0% of revenue on a commercial reserve release - below the 5.5% FY2027 assumption, but one quarter of releases is not a new mid-cycle rate); capital retention paths (FY2027 at 5% RWA growth - RWA grew 5.4% in nine months and marked CET1 is an estimated ~9.0%, below target, both of which argue for MORE retention or a slower buyback; held pending the FY2026 10-K and the 2027 capital plan, and flagged as the main downside to this update); SBC 1.6%; tax 21.0%; cost of equity 10.5% (see wacc_rationale: spot build-up is ~11.1%); terminal growth; scenario weights 20/50/30; historical growth (no new fiscal year). MODEL: Bank FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity on tangible book, run through the component engine (house precedent HBAN 2026-09-29, NAB.AX 2026-09-24, IAG.AX, GL). SKILL.md routes a bank to residual income on tangible book; FCFE with retention = NPAT x g/ROTE is the clean-surplus equivalent (FCFE = NPAT x (1 - g/ROTE)), and it goes through the validated slider engine, which also produces the workbook. An owner-FCF DCF on statutory cash flow is NOT used: KeyCorp's operating cash flow is loan/deposit movement and its long-term debt is operating funding, not net debt. Engine mapping: revenue = NII + noninterest income (GAAP); ebitda_margin_path = pre-tax income (revenue - noninterest expense - provision for credit losses) PLUS share-based compensation, as % of revenue (nine months 2026 actual: 5,945 - 3,643 - 259 = 2,043 = 34.4% + 1.7% SBC = 36.1%; FY2025: 32.6%; FY2026E: 8,075 - 4,923 - 359 = 2,793 = 34.6% + 1.6% = 36.2%); sbc_pct_path = 1.6%; da_pct = 0 (depreciation and software amortisation are inside noninterest expense and are genuine costs for a bank); capex_pct_path = capital RETAINED to fund RWA growth at the ~10% marked CET1 target = NPAT margin x balance-sheet growth / return on tangible equity; cash_tax_rate_path = 21.0% income tax; wacc = cost of equity 10.5%; net_debt = 0; equity_bridge = -1,975 preferred stock. FY2027 base reconciliation: 8,075 x 1.06 = 8,560 revenue x (36.5% - 1.6%) x (1 - 21%) = 2,360 GAAP net income, less ~117 preferred dividends = ~2,243 to common / 1,065m = ~$2.11 GAAP EPS (FY2025 actual $1.52; nine months 2026 $1.39; FY2026E ~$1.92), i.e. ~10% EPS growth. Residual-income cross-check on tangible book: base FY2027 ROTCE ~16.6% on ~$13.5bn of AOCI-marked TCE; P/TBV = (ROTCE - g)/(CoE - g) = (16.6 - 2.5)/(10.5 - 2.5) = 1.76x x $12.35 = ~$21.8/share, which the engine base approximates. The same value is ~1.37x ex-AOCI tangible book of ~$16.0, which is the more stable yardstick now that AOCI is ~$3.6/share. Price is the NYSE regular close, not an after-hours print. Clearwater UK closed in Q3 2026 (goodwill +$51m); its revenue is inside the FY2026E fee run-rate and no bridge item is carried.

bear.growth_rationale: The NIM recovery stalls: the Fed cuts faster than expected into a slowdown so the reinvestment yield on the repricing assets falls while deposit costs stay sticky, NIM plateaus at ~2.95% instead of expanding; investment-banking fees fall ~20% in a capital-markets downturn (the most cyclical fee line, ~12% of revenue); loan growth stops as commercial clients de-lever. Revenue +1% FY27, flat FY28, then 2-2.5% nominal.
bear.margin_rationale: FY27: efficiency 62.5% (revenue shortfall against a fixed cost base; FY2023 was 73.8% on the trough) - provision 8.0% (~55bp: CRE, agriculture and consumer-goods-linked commercial books management already flags as watch categories) + 1.6 = 31.1. FY28 credit cycle: provision 12.0% (~85bp; FY2020 was 1,021 = 15.2% of revenue, so this is a mid-sized cycle, not a crisis) with efficiency 63.0%: 26.6. Recovers to provision 8.0% and efficiency 62.0%: 31.6; then provision 7.0%, efficiency 61.0%: 33.6, held - no operating leverage, the efficiency ratio stays in KeyCorp's historical low-60s. FY27 GAAP EPS ~$1.65, FY28 ~$1.35; ROTCE ~10-11%, barely above the cost of equity. UPDATE 2026-11-19: every year lowered 0.2pt from the 2026-09-29 path for the cost of the wholesale funding that replaced the $525m Series D preferred redeemed on 15 Sep 2026 (~$17m/yr of pre-tax cost not yet in the FY2026E base = 0.2% of revenue); the efficiency and provision judgments above are otherwise unchanged, so each quoted build-up now sums 0.2pt above the path.
bear.capex_rationale: Retention = NPAT margin ~25% x g / ROTE ~10.5% = ~2.4 x g; FY27-29 held at 5.5% despite 0-2% growth because RWA migration and reserve build in a downturn consume capital the model must top up (marked CET1 ~9.8% is at the bottom of the 9.5-10% target range, so the 2023 precedent - a buyback halt, not a raise - repeats). Terminal 2% growth retains 4.8%.

base.growth_rationale: Total revenue. FY27 6.0%: full-year effect of the 3.00-3.05% Q4 2026 exit NIM against a ~2.95% FY26 average plus the remaining ~$9bn of low-yield fixed-rate assets repricing at ~1.25pts (management: NIM tailwinds continue through 2027) gives NII +6-7%; average loans +4-5% (commercial +8-10% guided for FY26 with consumer running off); fees +5% (KeyBanc Capital Markets pipeline, record AUM in wealth, first full year of Clearwater UK). Tapers to 2.5% terminal (nominal GDP less structural deposit-beta creep) once the repricing tailwind is exhausted by FY28.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-tax income + SBC on revenue. FY27 36.7% = 100 - GAAP efficiency 59.4% (FY26E ~60.9% = 4,870/8,000; expenses +3.5% against revenue +6% is the positive operating leverage management has delivered in 2025-26) - provision 5.5% (~40bp NCO on ~$112bn loans + reserve build for growth; FY26E 430 = 5.4%; H1 2026 ran 198 = 5.1% with releases) + SBC 1.6. Mature 37.6% = efficiency 58.0% (KeyCorp's structural efficiency is mid-to-high 50s at best - it has never sustained PNC's low-60s adjusted ratio at scale, so no further step-down) - provision 6.0% (mid-cycle ~45bp incl. builds; FY2025 6.3%, FY2019 7.0%, FY2018 3.8%) + 1.6. FY2025 actual was 32.6%; the path assumes the guided NIM recovery and expense discipline land. UPDATE 2026-11-19: every year lowered 0.2pt from the 2026-09-29 path for the cost of the wholesale funding that replaced the $525m Series D preferred redeemed on 15 Sep 2026 (~$17m/yr of pre-tax cost not yet in the FY2026E base = 0.2% of revenue); the efficiency and provision judgments above are otherwise unchanged, so each quoted build-up now sums 0.2pt above the path.
base.capex_rationale: Capital retained to hold marked CET1 at ~10% as RWA grows = NPAT margin (~27.7-28.4% of revenue) x balance-sheet growth / ROTE ~14.5% (total NI over TCE + preferred ~$17.5bn) = ~1.9 x g. FY27 at 5% RWA growth: 9.5% of revenue (~$805m, 34% of NPAT retained -> 66% distributed = $0.82 dividend ~$875m + ~$675m buybacks; the FY26 programme is larger because it is also returning the AOCI-accretion surplus). Steps down with balance-sheet growth (4.5% FY28, 4% FY29-30, 3.5%, 3%, 2.5% terminal) to 4.7% (~17% retained -> 83% distributed). Cross-check on CET1: 5% RWA growth on ~$15bn of marked CET1 capital needs ~$750m.

bull.growth_rationale: The Fed holds and the curve steepens, so the repricing tailwind lands at the top of the range and NIM exits 2027 above 3.20%; commercial loan growth runs 8-10% for a second year with deposit share gains funding it; KeyBanc Capital Markets and Clearwater ride a multi-year M&A upcycle with fees +10%; Scotiabank cross-border referrals begin to show. Revenue +8% FY27 fading to 3% terminal.
bull.margin_rationale: FY27: efficiency 58.5% (revenue +8% on expenses +3.5%) - provision 5.0% + 1.6 = 38.1. Positive operating leverage takes GAAP efficiency to 56.0% by FY30 with credit benign at ~5.0% of revenue (~38bp): 100 - 56.0 - 5.0 + 1.6 = 40.6, held. FY27 GAAP EPS ~$2.20, FY28 ~$2.45; ROTCE ~16-17%. UPDATE 2026-11-19: every year lowered 0.2pt from the 2026-09-29 path for the cost of the wholesale funding that replaced the $525m Series D preferred redeemed on 15 Sep 2026 (~$17m/yr of pre-tax cost not yet in the FY2026E base = 0.2% of revenue); the efficiency and provision judgments above are otherwise unchanged, so each quoted build-up now sums 0.2pt above the path.
bull.capex_rationale: Retention = NPAT margin ~30.8% x g / ROTE ~16% = ~1.9 x g: higher growth needs more capital even at a better return. FY27-28 at 6% RWA growth retains 11.6% of revenue (~38% of NPAT); terminal 3% growth retains 5.8% (~19%).

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: UNCHANGED at 20/50/30 on the Q3 2026 update; the evidence moved in both directions. House default is 15/50/35. Bear at 20%: KeyCorp's earnings are the most NIM-geared of the super-regional peer set, ~12% of revenue is cyclical investment-banking fees, and marked CET1 - ~9.8% at the prior build - is now an estimated ~9.0% after a $1.5bn AOCI move in Q3, below the 9.5-10% target, so the buyback is more exposed than it was. Not 25%: FY2026 guidance was tightened upward again in October (NII, loans), net charge-offs were guided down to 37-39bp, there is no acquisition integration, and unmarked CET1 is 11.08%. Bull at 30%: it needs a second year of 8-10% commercial loan growth, an M&A upcycle and an efficiency ratio KeyCorp has never sustained, all together; management's reaffirmed end-2027 targets sit between base and bull. What would move the weights: a buyback pause or a marked-CET1 disclosure below 9% (bear up), or FY2027 guidance that underwrites the 3.25% NIM target (bull up).
